decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, pens on the left. Begin a continuous elbow-up right-hand turn toward the holder, keeping the left arm clear.
Advance the right open gripper toward a side grasp on the holder while completing its inward turn; leave the pens undisturbed.
Bring the open right fingers forward and down alongside the upright holder; use the next wrist view to refine centering before closing.
The holder tipped during approach. Withdraw the right open fingers and raise for a clear view before recovering it upright.
Recover the fallen holder with an overhead grasp: raise and turn the right wrist while approaching from its own workspace, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
The turn was rejected without motion. Retry much smaller wrist increments while lifting, to preserve the current IK branch.
Continue the overhead recovery approach in small increments; keep the open gripper well above the fallen holder.
Align the right gripper above the fallen holder with its jaws across the holder's width; rotate gradually toward a downward approach.
The forward turn reached an IK limit. Retract the right arm toward the robot at constant height to recover elbow-up reach margin before continuing.
Retry the retraction with a 1.5 mm initial step and gradually increase only as the elbow moves away from its limit.
With reach margin restored, continue orienting the open right hand downward and shift toward the holder without crossing the centerline.
Finish the downward alignment and approach the holder's middle slowly; stop short of closing until the wrist view confirms the jaws straddle it.
Avoid extending farther at the wrist limit. Lower with the current oblique orientation toward the near end of the holder, using small continuous steps.
Close the right jaws around the near portion of the fallen holder, without further rotation. Retention will be checked during a small withdrawal.
Lift and retract the closed right gripper with the holder to create reach margin; check that the holder follows before attempting to upright it.
The holder did not follow the lift. Reopen and approach closer to its middle, farther forward and lower than the missed near-end grasp.
Use a shallower forward-reaching grasp rather than extend the elbow further. Retract the wrist slightly while lowering and tilting the open fingers toward the holder.
The holder now spans the wrist view between the open fingers. Make a small centering correction and close fully for a retention test.
The closed fingertips are still short of the holder. Reopen and advance carefully farther along its body, keeping the wrist low and the right arm on its own side.
The holder now extends through the open jaw region. Close fully in place, then make a small upward retention test before larger motion.
The last closure pushed the holder away instead of capturing it. Open and advance farther over the body with a small leftward correction, staying in the right workspace.
Use a small inward wrist turn instead of additional extension to engage the holder's near end, then close in place.
Test the near-end capture with a slow upward and backward motion, keeping the right gripper fully closed.
The holder has moved into the left-side reach and is still not captured. Clear the right arm and prepare the left hand to recover it from the accessible side.
Advance the left hand through its own workspace and turn it inward; the right hand stays clear while planning a side capture of the fallen holder.
Replan with smaller left-arm increments after the continuity stop, rolling the open jaws for a side-on holder grasp while advancing slowly.
Reduce the left wrist roll and translation further to maintain joint continuity while moving toward the holder.
Approach from the left-front with an oblique downward grip, keeping the jaws horizontal across the holder rather than pushing its end.
Continue the left-front approach above the pens, keeping the right hand stationary and clear.
Advance the left open jaws toward the holder's near end while lowering to its side height; preserve the current horizontal jaw alignment.
The holder is left of the open-jaw center. Shift the left hand laterally toward it and slightly lower to center the near end between the fingers.
Refine lateral alignment on the holder's visible base, then advance a short distance with the jaws fully open.
The base is centered between the jaws. Advance along the holder axis to surround the base, then close fully without further translation.
The holder is now surrounded by the left fingers. Lift and retract with full closure to verify capture and create space to restore it upright.
The holder followed the left-hand lift. Begin rotating its open end upward while preparing the right hand for a side support grasp, with both wrists staying on their own sides.
The visible hexagonal face is the closed base, so reverse the pivot to bring the opening upward. Raise for clearance and finish the right side-grasp orientation.
Continue the controlled pivot and lift the holder farther from the table. Move the right hand outward so it cannot obstruct the recovery rotation.

Roll the retained holder about the finger approach axis, keeping its base position steady, to turn the closed base downward and the opening upward.
Continue rolling the held cup toward opening-up, lowering the wrist slightly to retain clearance and reach margin. Keep the right hand clear.
Roll the cup farther toward vertical while keeping its grasp steady; use the head view to check which end is uppermost before transferring support.
Correct the remaining forward lean of the held cup while lowering it to a reachable transfer height. Bring the right open gripper closer, stopping outside the cup.
The opening is now visibly uppermost. Keep the left base grasp steady and align the right open jaws around the cup's middle for support transfer.
Relieve contact by raising the right jaws slightly, center them farther forward around the cup, and close while the left hand continues supporting the base.
The right closure was above the cup body. Reopen and lower the grasp, centering farther forward while the left hand retains the upright holder.
Settle the right fingers slightly lower and close around the upper body, retaining the left base support until the transfer can be checked visually.
Release the left base support and withdraw it slowly while the closed right hand lifts the upright holder, checking that it follows the right grasp.
The right hand did not retain the cup. Clear it and reapproach the fallen holder with the left hand, using its accessible near end.
Lower the inverted left jaws to the fallen holder's base height and refine centering, keeping the right hand clear.
Close around the centered near end without pressing farther down, then make a small lift to check retention.
The holder remained beyond the fingertips. Reopen and advance farther around its near end without pushing farther into the table.
Advance a short distance to seat the holder deeper between the left fingers, then close in place for another capture check.
Lift and retract the closed left hand gently to check whether the near-end capture retains the holder.
The holder slipped into the right workspace. Clear the left arm and bring the right open side grasp forward and down toward the holder's body.
The holder is below and forward of the right-jaw center. Lower and shift forward slowly to straddle its body with the open fingers.
Avoid further table contact by raising the wrist and tilting the open fingers down and forward toward the holder's center.
The turn was rejected without motion. First withdraw a little to restore joint margin, then use much smaller downward wrist increments.
Continue the small oblique wrist turn to bring the holder between the right jaws, lifting the wrist enough to avoid scraping the table.
Center the right jaws on the holder's visible middle with a small forward and downward correction before closing.
The holder's length spans the jaws, so this side approach cannot enclose it. Withdraw and turn toward an overhead grasp across its width.
Continue turning the right hand downward with extra reach margin, aligning the jaw-closing direction across the holder rather than along its length.

Avoid pressing vertically against the table. Tilt the fingers forward and center them farther left to reach around the holder's near half.
The holder is now seated deeper between the right fingers. Close fully, settle, and make a small upward/backward retention test.

Shift the right open jaws laterally onto the holder's near end and angle the fingertips slightly downward, keeping the wrist on the right side.
Aim the right fingers farther left by yawing rather than crossing the wrist over the centerline, then close around the near end.
Keep the right fingers closed and test the near-end capture with a gentle lift and retraction.

Continue around the holder's right end with the open gripper, keeping a continuous elbow-up path and avoiding another lengthwise closure.
Bring the right fingers farther forward toward the holder's right end with a slight oblique yaw, avoiding a straight overextended reach.
Restore reach margin after the guard by drawing the wrist back, while yawing the open fingers toward the holder's visible end.
Move outward on the right and turn back toward the holder's right end, rather than attempting to close across its full length.
Use a diagonal approach to the right end, bringing the fingers forward while preserving wrist reach margin. Keep the jaws open for centering.
At the current reach limit, close on the accessible end and test a short lift and withdrawal rather than extend farther.
